requirement_text.REQ-001b: Extract remaining hardcoded copy from all 12 landing components into messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json, wire via next-intl getTranslations/t.rich(). 5 acceptance criteria: (1) no hardcoded Cyrillic remains in the 12 components; (2) matching 177-key catalogs; (3) every new uz value non-empty; (4) clean build; (5) both /ru and /uz render all 12 sections with no missing-key errors.

result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-001b end-to-end on branch feature/WF02-REQ-001b, not trusting TEST-RUNNER's report -- re-ran every check myself with my own commands/scripts and got identical results throughout. (1) npm run lint: exit 0, 0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings (next/image suggestions in Avatar.jsx/Footer.tsx/Nav.tsx, one unused var in an unrelated docs/ design-system file) -- none reference i18n. (2) npm run build: exit 0, '✓ Compiled successfully', TypeScript finished with no Type error, route table includes 'ƒ /[locale]' and 'ƒ Proxy (Middleware)'; re-ran a second time piping stdout+stderr to a log and grep -i error over it produced zero matches (grep exit 1). (3) Wrote and ran my own Cyrillic-sweep node script (Unicode range /[Ѐ-ӿ]/) over all 12 landing components: files_scanned=12, cyrillic_matches=[]; companion grep -l getTranslations across the same 12 files returned exactly 12. (4) Wrote and ran my own key-set-diff node script over messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json: ru_count=177, uz_count=177, key_sets_match=true, in_ru_not_uz=[], in_uz_not_ru=[]; same script's empty-value check found empty_uz_values=[] across all 177 uz keys. (5) Built and started the production server myself on port 3101 (npm run build && npm run start -- -p 3101, backgrounded), confirmed 200 on /ru within ~4s, and independently curled: no MISSING_MESSAGE/IntlError markers on /ru or /uz (grep exit 1 both); Hero.eyebrow flat key identical on both locales ('AI Qadam · UZ · KZ · KG · TJ'); Team.team1Name repeated-array item identical on both locales ('Бинали Рустамов'); both t.rich() emphasis cases (Hero.title, Creed.quote) rendered real <em> tags identically on /ru and /uz, and the negative check for escaped '<em>' found none; both locales returned HTTP 200; all 6 landmark selectors present exactly once each on /ru; <section> count was exactly 10 on both /ru and /uz. Killed the server afterward and confirmed the port's LISTENING entry was gone (curl to it returned HTTP_CODE:000). All 5 of REQ-001b's acceptance criteria are confirmed against actual current code/output: AC1 (no hardcoded Cyrillic remains, all 12 wired to getTranslations) CONFIRMED; AC2 (matching 177-key catalogs) CONFIRMED; AC3 (every new uz value non-empty) CONFIRMED; AC4 (clean build) CONFIRMED; AC5 (/ru and /uz render all 12 sections, no missing-key errors) CONFIRMED. requirements.yaml staleness check: reviewed docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-001b entry (description + 5 acceptance_criteria) against FRONTEND-DEV's 2 reported MINOR deviations (indexed-key naming for MapSection/Streams/Metrics arrays; Streams' foundationTitle/foundationLink extracted per the design table's literal listing), both already reviewed and accepted by REVIEWER as defensible judgment calls, not violations. Neither deviation is asserted one way or the other anywhere in requirements.yaml's REQ-001b text -- the entry describes desired outcome (extract copy, wire via next-intl, matching key sets, non-empty uz values, clean build, both locales render) and testable criteria, never specific key names or a brand/URL-classification rule for individual components. Both deviations are implementation details squarely inside the requirement's existing degrees of freedom. Conclusion: requirements.yaml's REQ-001b entry needs NO correction -- nothing in it is rendered stale or inaccurate by what actually shipped.
